FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
When a commercial rig approaches from the opposite way, hug the right edge so the two vehicles never sideswipe [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
Big rigs often swing wide left before a right turn, so never squeeze between the rig and the curb where its driver cannot see you [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
Never cross behind a commercial vehicle that is backing up or about to back up, because its bulk hides everything behind it [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A01
Before passing a rig, check ahead and behind, enter the passing lane only when it is clear and safe, signal the lane change, and blink your headlights to warn its driver [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A01
Pass commercial vehicles on the left for best visibility and finish the pass fast instead of cruising in their blind spots [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A01
Never cut back too soon after passing a rig since it brakes slower than cars; wait until you see its cab in your rear-view mirror, and note its driver may flash headlights when merging back is safe [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A01
Skip passing a commercial vehicle on a downgrade, where its weight and momentum keep gaining speed [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A01
While a commercial vehicle passes you, stay on the right side of your lane and never speed up [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A01
Drivers, bicyclists, and walkers must all yield to police cars, fire engines, and other emergency vehicles running sirens or flashing lights [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A01
At the approach of an emergency vehicle, pull to the nearest road edge at once and stop until it passes, keeping every intersection clear [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A01
Yield to funeral processions; after the lead car enters an intersection, the rest of the line may follow through no matter what the signals or signs say [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A01
Every car in a funeral line runs headlights or flashing hazard lights, and other drivers must never cut into the procession [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A02
Golf carts belong only on golf courses or roadways posted for them with proper signs [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A02
Drivers under age 18 need a valid learner license or driver license to take a cart onto a public road, and drivers 18 or older must hold valid government-issued photo identification [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A02
A cart may not run at all in a county or city that has not expressly allowed it [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A02
Carts run only between sunrise and sunset unless the local government authorizes night driving with added equipment [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A02
A cart may cross a state road only where the posted limit is 45 MPH or less and only at an intersection with a traffic control device [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A02
Carts may use a sidewalk at least 5 feet wide, always yielding to people on foot [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A02
Cart drivers obey every state and local traffic law, including yielding the right-of-way [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A02
Every cart needs efficient brakes, a rear-view mirror, reliable steering, red warning reflectors front and rear, and safe tires [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A02
Child passenger seats must stay off golf carts and other low-speed vehicles because they are never crash-tested for them and may fail; follow the seat maker guidance [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A02
Night cart driving demands headlights, brake lights, turn signals, and a windshield [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A02
Low-speed vehicles run on four wheels with top speeds from 21 to 25 MPH, converted carts qualify, and every operator needs a valid driver license [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A02
Low-speed vehicles stay on streets posted 35 MPH or less, must carry headlamps, stop lamps, turn signals, tail lamps, reflectors, parking brakes, rear-view mirrors, a windshield, safety belts, and a vehicle identification number, and must be registered and properly insured [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A02
Motorcycle and moped riders keep the same road rights and duties as car drivers and face citations for violations [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-F26 | anchor: A02
A motorist must never split a lane with a motorcycle, whose rider is entitled to the whole lane [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0093]
